messages:
elaine-sales: Heads-up: NovaHealth POC wants Private deployment in their AWS account + onprem proxy. Need clear checklist: VPC endpoints (PrivateLink), NAT mapping for preserve client IP, firewall allowlist, and whether reserved egress IPs cost extra. @devon-netops @leia-sec

 devon-netops: Got it. Quick Qs: Are they planning ENIs in each AZ or using single interface endpoint per service? If multi-AZ, we'll recommend NLB-backed interface endpoints. Also need their VPC CIDR(s) and onprem egress ranges.

 elaine-sales: They'll do multi-AZ. VPC CIDRs: 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/16. Onprem NAT ranges TBD (we'll get them). Can you draft firewall snippet and NAT mapping guidance?

 devon-netops: Sure. Basic firewall egress rules:

 ```
 # Allow outbound to Redwood control plane (TLS)
 ALLOW TCP 443 to 52.41.123.45/32  # control-plane.example.redwood.com

 # PrivateLink interface endpoints (DNS over ENI)
 ALLOW TCP 443 to vpce-* ENIs in their VPC

 # If using proxy/NAT: preserve SNI by allowing CONNECT passthrough
 ALLOW TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 with SNI passthrough
 ```

 devon-netops: For NAT mapping and src-IP preservation: if they require original client IP for audit, we recommend deploying our SNI-preserving proxy in their VPC (via our Private Deploy package) or use an NLB with proxy protocol. If they must route via corporate NAT, map 1:1 sticky EIPs to each connector instance.

 leia-sec: Security checklist: SOC2 type II? encryption in transit & at rest required? Will they use KMS? We need answers on data residency and bring-your-own-key (BYOK). Also need to confirm whether their proxy performs TLS interception (TLS-inspect) — that changes cert requirements.

 elaine-sales: They're SOC2 and want BYOK / KMS. No TLS inspection on their side (no MITM) — they want end-to-end TLS.

 raj-eng: Important: for Private Deploy control plane reachability we need outbound to our control-plane IPs plus access to model shard egress for updates. Typical ports:
 - TCP 443 to control-plane
 - TCP 80/443 for image downloads (optional)

 raj-eng: If using PrivateLink, DNS resolution for our service will point to ENI IPs; ensure their Route53 private hosted zone doesn't override those. Also add these SRV records:

 ```
 redwood-control.redwood.internal -> vpce-abcde.local
 ```

 sam-salesops: Pricing note: Reserved egress IPs (sticky EIP add-on) are +$250/mo per IP for POC usage. If they need >5 IPs we can discount. SNI-preserving proxy appliance is an additional one-time setup fee of $5k for onprem integration.

 elaine-sales: Copy. Can you draft an answer for their security questionnaire re: network flow and BYOK, @leia-sec?

 leia-sec: Draft coming. Start language:
 "Network flow: All customer traffic to Redwood Private Deploy is over TLS 1.2+ to customer-managed PrivateLink endpoints. Customer keys are stored in their KMS; we do not have access to plaintext model inputs when BYOK enabled. Control-plane calls are authenticated with mTLS and logged."

 elaine-sales: Perfect. One blocker from procurement: they want guarantee that no egress to external IPs outside allowed list occurs during POC. Is there a hard egress lock-down mode?

 devon-netops: We have an egress whitelist mode in Private Deploy that restricts outbound to a configured set of CIDRs (control plane + model artifact sources + optional metrics endpoints). It will fail closed if other egress attempted. Need to enable at deploy time and provide the whitelist CIDR list.

 elaine-sales: Great. Timeline: POC kickoff Wed. Can we have config doc + firewall snippet by EOD tomorrow?

 devon-netops: I'll drop a short runbook into the onboarding doc. :thumbsup:

 deploy-bot: New ticket created: RDW-POC-9812 assigned to devon-netops, due 2 days.

 elaine-sales: Thanks all — I'll update NovaHealth and collect NAT ranges from them.
